gaps: Apidog project for RunCloud v3 lists 222 endpoints; this spec covers ~143 (PHP SDK action map plus 13 v3-newer endpoints confirmed during research: WAF install, RunCloudHub install, v3 Create Server, full backups to RunCloud/local storage, S3 storage integration, WordPress one-shot create). Residual gap ~80 endpoints expected to be: WAF CRUD verbs beyond install (~7-10), RunCloudHub status/update/uninstall (~3-5), Backups list/restore/delete/history/db-only/file-only (~15-20), agency-api workspace/billing/additional team ops (~20-30), notification/webhook subscriptions, container-stack operations. v0.2 reprint via /printing-press-amend or /printing-press --spec <apidog-export> when Apidog export becomes possible.
Apidog project at https://app.apidog.com/project/600229 — user-confirmed but locked to login; not exportable from current UI.
patterns: Two API surfaces (agency-api / core-api) share the same bearer token; agency-api lives under /agency.
Pagination: page + perPage (max 40). Auto-paginate via --all flag.

novel_features.name: Fleet SSL audit
novel_features.description: Find every SSL certificate across every server that is missing, expiring soon, or already expired — one query, whole fleet.
novel_features.rationale: Joins synced webapps × domains × ssl_certs in local SQLite. The v3 API is server-keyed and cannot answer 'fleet-wide cert state' in one request.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Agents auditing certificate hygiene get a deterministic table instead of having to fan out N parallel /servers/{id}/webapps/{id}/ssl calls.

novel_features.name: Reverse domain lookup
novel_features.description: Given a domain (or pattern), return the server, webapp, system user, and SSL config that hosts it.
novel_features.rationale: FTS5 over local mirror of domains/webapps/servers. The dashboard requires you to already know which server hosts a domain — circular for new operators.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Maps a domain to its operational context in one call — essential before any cross-resource action.

novel_features.name: Fleet PHP version audit
novel_features.description: Find every webapp running below a given PHP version, grouped by server.
novel_features.rationale: Joins servers.phpCliVersion + webapps.phpVersion from synced store with SemVer comparison.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pre-upgrade scoping; current alternative is opening every server's PHP tab.

novel_features.name: Fleet health roll-up
novel_features.description: Show uptime, load, disk, and memory for every server in one comparable table, powered by v3's new /health/latest endpoint.
novel_features.rationale: Fan-out + cache + bounded under IsDogfoodEnv. v3 ships /servers/{id}/health/latest as a snapshot-friendly source, replacing v2's /stats.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Monday-morning fleet glance — one read instead of N dashboard tabs.

novel_features.name: Fleet blocked-IPs dedupe
novel_features.description: Show every fail2ban-blocked IP across the fleet, deduped, with server count, first seen, and last seen.
novel_features.rationale: The same attacker IP appearing on 5 servers is 5 separate dashboard clicks today; aggregates synced fail2ban rows into a keyed local view.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Identify pattern attackers and shared-blocklist candidates in one query.

novel_features.name: Fleet WordPress/CMS inventory
novel_features.description: List every webapp that has a script-installer attached (WordPress, Joomla, Drupal, etc.) with version and site URL.
novel_features.rationale: Joins per-webapp /installer results across the fleet. RunCloud's core identity is WordPress hosting — the dashboard refuses to assemble this view.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Find every WordPress site for compliance, version sweeps, or plugin auditing.

novel_features.name: Agency client onboarding chain
novel_features.description: Onboard a new agency client end-to-end: create client → assign server-package → spin up client-server → optional magic link. Emits a credentials summary.
novel_features.rationale: v3 introduces the agency-api workspace surface that v2 did not have. This chains create-client + create-client-server + create-client-magic-link with credential summary.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Replaces a multi-modal dashboard flow with one scripted command — essential for agencies running v3's reseller features.

novel_features.name: Fleet SSH-key audit
novel_features.description: Inventory every SSH key across every (server, system_user) pair, deduped by fingerprint.
novel_features.rationale: Quarterly key rotation requires this and the API gives only one-server-one-user lists today.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Find stale keys, identify shared keys across users, prepare for rotation.

novel_features.name: Fleet stale services
novel_features.description: Filter every server's services list for non-running rows or a named service across the whole fleet.
novel_features.rationale: 'Is nginx running everywhere?' should be one command, not 12.
novel_features.why_it_matters: On-call ritual — instant verification that critical services are up across the fleet.

narrative.headline: Fleet-wide visibility for RunCloud v3 — every SSL cert, PHP version, blocked IP, and SSH key across the whole workspace in one command.
narrative.value_prop: RunCloud's dashboard is per-server. This CLI mirrors the v3 API into a local SQLite store and gives you the cross-server queries the dashboard refuses to assemble: `fleet ssl-audit` for cert expiry across the fleet, `whois-fleet` for domain → server reverse lookup, `fleet health` powered by v3's new /health/latest endpoint, and `fleet blocked-ips` for fail2ban dedupe. v3's agency-api workspace surface is exposed under `runcloud-pp-cli agency` with a chained `agency onboard` command for new-client provisioning. WordPress one-shot provisioning rides v3's native `POST /webapps/wordpress` endpoint via `webapps create-wordpress`.
narrative.auth_narrative: RunCloud v3 uses bearer-token auth. Generate a token from Workspace > Settings > API Management, then export `RUNCLOUD_API_TOKEN` (or pass `--api-key`). v2's key:secret pair is no longer accepted.

quickstart.comment: Verify the bearer token resolves and /ping responds.
Mirror every server, webapp, domain, database, and SSH key into local SQLite.
First-week-of-the-month ritual: certs expiring in the next month.
Find which server hosts a domain — the dashboard makes you already know.
Monday glance — uptime/load/disk/memory across the fleet, one read.

troubleshoots.fix: Bearer token missing or invalid. Generate a new one from Workspace > Settings > API Management and `export RUNCLOUD_API_TOKEN=...`. v2 key:secret pairs do not work in v3.
Check `X-RateLimit-Remaining`. Reduce `--per-page`, batch with `--all` more slowly, or use the local store via `runcloud-pp-cli search`/`sql` instead of live API.
Run `runcloud-pp-cli sync --full` first — fleet queries read from the local store, not the live API.
Names resolve through FTS over the synced store. Either run `sync` or use the numeric webapp ID.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when you operate more than one RunCloud server and have to ask fleet-wide questions the dashboard cannot answer in one click — SSL expiry across servers, PHP version compliance, fail2ban dedupe, WordPress site inventory, domain reverse lookup. Also use it for one-shot WordPress provisioning and (on v3 agency plans) chained client onboarding. Pair it with `--json`/`--select` for agentic workflows that need to feed RunCloud state into downstream automation.

recipes.title: Monday SSL sweep
recipes.explanation: Every webapp/domain whose cert expires in the next month, agent-shaped output for piping into a renewal script.

recipes.title: Domain-to-server reverse lookup
recipes.explanation: Find which server + webapp + system user + SSL config hosts `example.com` — answer the question the dashboard makes you already know.

recipes.title: Spin up a WordPress site (v3 native)
recipes.command: runcloud-pp-cli webapps create-wordpress --server-id 42 --name client-site --domain-name example.com --site-title 'Client Site' --admin-username wpadmin --admin-email admin@example.com --password ChangeMeStrongPwd123
recipes.explanation: Single call to v3's POST /servers/{id}/webapps/wordpress — creates the webapp, database, db user, and grant atomically. Add `webapps ssl install` as a follow-up if you want HTTPS.

recipes.title: Onboard a new agency client
recipes.explanation: v3 agency-api chain: create-client → create-client-server → optional magic-link; emits credentials summary.

recipes.title: Friday security sweep
recipes.explanation: Every fail2ban-blocked IP across the fleet from the last week, deduped with `servers_count` to find pattern attackers.
